subject: Session snapshot retention, no-train commitment & escrow ask
messages:
From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@carepointhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@carepointhealth.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Session snapshot retention, training exclusion and escrow ask

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Security and procurement at CarePoint asked me to follow up with a few specific asks before we move forward with a pilot:

1) A firm no-training / no-model-improvement commitment on any patient or PHI-derived content.
2) Operational evidence for session-snapshot retention: what artifacts you store, for how long, and how customers can request deletion or exports.
3) A path for escrow/transfer of session snapshots or transcript archives (we have some internal policy that prefers an escrow option when vendor data retention exceeds 90 days).
4) If retention/escrow commitments are breached, confirmation of SLA credits and a rollback/restore mechanism to revert to the model state prior to the breach.

I've attached a short PDF of the security team's questions (CarePoint_DPA_questions.pdf). Can you provide a short ops summary and a proposed contractual addendum we can share with legal? We need this to close procurement next month.

Appreciate a clear list of deliverables and an ETA.

Best,
Ethan Morales
Senior IT Security Manager
CarePoint Health

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Kim (privacy/contracts) and Laura (ops) so we can give a consolidated response. High level:

- Redwood can commit to a contractual no-training clause (we will not use customer prompts/responses to improve models) for CarePoint under a DPA addendum.
- Operationally, session snapshots (transcripts, metadata, ephemeral KV cache dumps) are kept by default for a configurable retention period; we can offer a 30-day standard retention window for PHI-bearing sessions and provide an export on request.
- We don't currently provide a long-term escrow of raw session archives as a standard product, but we can propose an escrow workflow with SFTP or encrypted archive transfer for audit/backup purposes. Laura: could you outline the minimal ops evidence we can deliver (logs, manifest, retention export) and a timeline?

Next steps proposal:
- Laura to send an ops evidence spreadsheet with fields we can deliver (audit log extract, deletion report, export manifest).
- Kim to draft DPA addendum language covering no-train, deletion/export SLA, subprocessor notice, and an escrow clause option.
- I can provide a short note on rollback/restore expectations from a serving/runtime perspective (model pinning and snapshot revert).

ETA: I can get the ops evidence and draft addendum over the next 6 business days if that works for your procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Sales partner)
Redwood Inference

Ethan / team —

Quick ops summary and what we can produce as discrete artifacts:

Deliverables we can provide within 5 business days:
- Audit log extract (timestamped request IDs, route, model variant, region).
- Export manifest (list of files and hashes for any session archive we deliver).
- Deletion certificate (time-stamped confirmation when a snapshot is purged).
- KV/cache eviction report (if customers use ephemeral-session mode).

Retention options:
- Default: 30 days for PHI sessions (configurable to shorter via account settings).
- Long-term: we can create an encrypted export and deliver via SFTP or customer-managed storage; delivery takes 2–4 business days once requested and signed off by legal.

Escrow / rollback notes:
- We can support one-off escrow exports (encrypted tarball + manifest). Redwood can also provide a copy to a third-party escrow agent on request; that will require an addendum covering escrow agent access and s3/SFTP endpoint details.
- For rollback: our serving runtime supports model pinning. If a retention breach required rollback, we can pin a previous model checkpoint and restore the environment for traffic routing within 8 business hours for dedicated accounts; hosted API responses may require a 24–72 hour cutover depending on routing and regional caches.

Attached is a small spreadsheet (redwood-session-retention-ops.xlsx) with fields we will populate for the audit bundle.

Laura Bennett
Senior Ops Manager, Customer Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Session snapshot retention, training exclusion and escrow ask

Ethan —

Draft DPA addendum highlights attached (proposed-dpa-addendum.docx). Key commercial/legal points we recommend: 

- No-Training Commitment: Insert explicit clause: "Vendor shall not use Customer data (prompts, responses, transcripts) to train, fine-tune, or improve any model or algorithm without Customer's prior written consent."
- Export & Deletion SLA: Vendor to provide export within 7 business days and deletion confirmation within 5 business days of a lawful request.
- Subprocessor Disclosure: Redwood will list subprocessors and provide 30 days' notice for material changes; customers may request a subprocessor freeze during active pilot/procurement.
- Escrow Option: Customer may request an encrypted escrow export; Redwood will execute transfer with manifest and provide hash-based integrity check. Costs: escrow exports will be included for enterprise pilots; ongoing escrow storage managed by the customer thereafter.
- SLA credits: For confirmed breaches of retention/export obligations, proposed credit of 10% of monthly committed fees for each occurrence up to a cap (negotiable).

I included suggested language for the rollback/restore mechanism that ties to model pinning and an operational incident process (we'll need to align runbooks).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Session snapshot retention, training exclusion and escrow ask

Team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft addendum. A few clarifying points from procurement/security before we route to legal: 

- The no-train clause language looks good; we need explicit confirmation that subcontractors (subprocessors) will also be bound by the same no-train prohibition for CarePoint data.
- Export SLA: 7 business days is acceptable for pilot; can you confirm the export includes an integrity manifest and that transfers will be encrypted in transit (SFTP/TLS) and at rest (AES-256)?
- Escrow: CarePoint prefers Redwood to push an encrypted archive to our SFTP escrow endpoint (we will provide credentials post-SOW). Please confirm a test transfer during pilot.
- SLA credits: we'd like the credit to be triggered for a failure to produce the export or deletion confirmation within the SLA window; the 10% cap is acceptable as a starting point but please mark negotiable.

If you can confirm subprocessors will be contractually constrained and provide the ops evidence bundle (audit log, manifest, deletion certificate) we'll start routing the addendum through our legal/compliance next week.

Best,
Ethan
Senior IT Security Manager
CarePoint Health
